what_it_does: Running large AI language models as cloud services for conversational agents and assistants is expensive, partly because generating each new word (the 'decode' phase) is bottlenecked by how fast the chip can read model weights from memory rather than by raw arithmetic speed. SambaNova's SN40L chip uses a 'dataflow' architecture — instead of a general-purpose processor fetching and executing instructions one by one, the computation graph of the entire model is mapped directly onto reconfigurable circuits so data flows through fixed paths with minimal overhead, similar to an assembly line. This lets the chip fuse many separate computation steps into single efficient passes, boosting word-generation speed. The chip also has three tiers of memory built in: fast on-chip storage (similar to a CPU's cache), high-bandwidth memory (fast but limited-capacity memory stacked on the chip), and standard off-chip DRAM (large but slower), allowing it to hold the weights for many different models simultaneously and switch between them rapidly to serve diverse agents. This paper is an invited industry overview describing the architecture and its deployment in SambaNova's inference cloud.
